title: Probabilities of the two signs sum to one
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$. The uniform probabilities that $f$ equals $1$ and that $f$ equals $-1$ sum to $1$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the sign cube of dimension $n$ to $\{−1,1\}$
